label: myadhd.my
caption:
Dentist at 4pm. So nothing else happens today.

That is waiting mode, and a lot of ADHD brains live in it. Swipe for why one appointment can hold a whole day hostage, and three ways to get the hours back.

If this sounded like your brain, come sit with people who get it. Our group is in my bio 👇

Save this for the next day with a 4pm in it.

#adhd #adhdmalaysia #myadhd #adhdadult #waitingmode

slides.title:
Why does one
[[4pm]] eat my
whole day?
slides.sub: You are not wasting the day. You are guarding it.

slides.title:
You are on
[[standby]]
until 4
slides.body: An appointment later today, and the hours before it go grey. You could start something. You do not. Anything you start might make you late.

slides.title:
Starting feels
[[risky]]
slides.body: If you get absorbed, you might lose track and miss it. So your brain plays safe and picks nothing. It looks like idleness. It is self-protection.

slides.title:
Waiting is
still [[work]]
slides.body: Checking the clock every ten minutes takes effort. By the time the appointment comes, you are tired from a day where nothing happened.

slides.title:
It comes from
[[losing time]]
before
slides.body: After years of running late without meaning to, you stop trusting your sense of time. Waiting mode is your brain refusing to get caught out again.

slides.title:
Set [[two]]
alarms, then
let go
slides.body: One for getting ready, one for leaving. Now watching the clock is the alarm's job, not yours, and the hours before are free again.

slides.title:
Pick a task
with a [[clean]]
stop
slides.body: Laundry, a short email, a walk round the block. Things that end on their own are safer than a rabbit hole before 4pm.

slides.title:
Book things
[[early]] when
you can
slides.body: A 9am appointment leaves the rest of the day open. Put errands on the same day, so the other days stay clear.

slides.title:
Save this for the
next day with a
[[4pm]] in it
slides.body: The waiting is real, and it is not laziness. Dump the day into my.adhd and get one thing back that fits before you go.
